newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt says no decision on GST referendum.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt says no decision on GST referendum.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Monday the government had taken no decision about the possibility of holding a referendum on a goods and services tax (GST).
"The position of the government is that it will take advice from all sources before announcing its position," Costello told parliament.
Costello said the government was currently considering several tax reform proposals but the only decision it had made at this stage was that the tax system needed to be overhauled.
"There is no particular significance to be attached to any of the proposals," Costello said.
"But the one thing the government has decided, of course, is that the government will support tax reform."
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith on Sunday raised the possibility of holding a national referendum on the introduction of a consumption tax.
The government began talking about reforming the tax system last month, and although it has not outlined policies at this stage, it appears to favour a consumption tax.
A GST is a consumption tax that is paid by consumers when they buy a good or service.
But the government remains committed to not imposing a GST in its first three-year term.

The Liberal-National government won power in 1996 after dropping an earlier policy to levy a 15 percent GST -- a policy widely blamed for the conservatives losing what was regarded as an unloseable election in 1993. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
